2027-03-12.title: Friday of the fifth week of the Great Fast
readings: Abraham pays the full price for the field of Ephron
Christ is our peace: the dividing wall broken down
Beware the yeast; do you not yet understand?
2027-03-12.alt: Great Fast (Valiya Nombu), fifth week. A Friday of the Great Fast: abstinence and the Way of the Cross, as is the custom of our parishes. Next Friday, 19 March, is the Fortieth Friday.
2027-03-12.verse: For he is our peace; in his flesh he has made both groups into one and has broken down the dividing wall, that is, the hostility between us.
theo: The negotiation at Hebron is told in slow, careful detail, at the city gate, “in the hearing of the Hittites.” Ephron makes a generous public offer: “No, my lord, hear me; I give you the field, and I give you the cave that is in it… bury your dead.” Abraham bows, and refuses the gift: “I will give the price of the field; accept it from me, so that I may bury my dead there.” Ephron names the price as if it were nothing, “four hundred shekels of silver, what is that between you and me?”, and Abraham pays it in full, “according to the weights current among the merchants.” Why does Genesis care so much? Because this is the first piece of the promised land that belongs to Abraham, and it must be his openly, justly and beyond dispute. He will not hold God's promise on a borrowed title or leave a debt behind his wife's grave. Centuries later King David says the same when he buys the threshing floor for the altar: “I will not offer burnt offerings to the Lord my God that cost me nothing.” Honest dealing in money and property is part of holiness, and the Great Fast is a good time to set right any unpaid debt, unfair price or unclear boundary.

Abraham bought a field with silver; Christ bought a people with his blood. St Paul reminds the Christians of Ephesus, Gentiles by birth, that they were once “without Christ, being aliens from the commonwealth of Israel, and strangers to the covenants of promise, having no hope and without God in the world. But now in Christ Jesus you who once were far off have been brought near by the blood of Christ. For he is our peace.” The dividing wall that Christ broke down is the hostility between peoples, and above all between each of us and God; on the Cross he reconciled “both groups to God in one body.” The Gentiles do not replace Israel; they are brought near to share its promises, “citizens with the saints and also members of the household of God, built upon the foundation of the apostles and prophets, with Christ Jesus himself as the cornerstone.” St John Chrysostom compared this to melting a statue of silver and a statue of lead together and drawing out from the fire a single statue of gold: Christ does not merely put two peoples side by side but makes of them something new (in substance). In the Gospel the disciples have “only one loaf with them in the boat,” and when Jesus warns them, “beware of the yeast of the Pharisees and the yeast of Herod,” they think only of bread. Yeast is a small hidden thing that spreads through the whole batch: the leaven of hardness of heart and of worldly power can enter any of us. Jesus asks: “Are your hearts hardened? Do you have eyes, and fail to see?… Do you not yet understand?” The one Loaf in the boat was Jesus himself, who had fed thousands and would give his Body on the Cross.

live: Before Easter, pay one debt, return one borrowed thing, or set right one unfair deal.
Make peace this week with one person or family with whom you have a quarrel.
2027-03-12.prayer: Lord Jesus Christ, by your blood you brought near those who were far off, and on the Cross you broke down the dividing wall of hostility. Make us honest in our dealings like Abraham, peacemakers in our homes and parishes, and free from the yeast of hypocrisy and the love of power. Open our eyes to see you, the one Bread in our boat. Amen.
altar: At the altar the Body broken on the Cross makes us one body, reconciled to God and to one another.

quick: Ephron offered the field as a gift; Abraham insisted on paying the full price of four hundred shekels.
Christ is our peace: by his blood those who were far off are brought near and made members of God's household.
Jesus warned against the yeast of the Pharisees and of Herod and asked: “Do you not yet understand?”
2027-03-12.action: Make peace with one person before Sunday.
2027-03-12.question: What wall have I built between myself and someone else?

family.explain: St Paul says that Jesus is our peace. He broke down the wall that kept people apart and made us all one family in God's house. Sometimes we build walls in our family when we are angry and do not speak to each other. Jesus helps us to break them down.
family.intention: We pray for families and neighbours who are quarrelling.
family.ask: Ask: “Is there anyone we need to make peace with this week?”

illus: Two brothers in a village near Adoor had not spoken for eleven years because of a strip of land between their houses, less than two metres wide. A wall of hollow blocks stood on it. One Lent their mother, who was very ill, asked to be carried to the parish for the Way of the Cross. At the twelfth station she asked her sons to stand on either side of her. When she came home she said: I have one request before I die. Within a month the wall was down. The strip of land is now a path where their grandchildren run between the two houses.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you are our peace. Break down the walls in our hearts and in our homes. Amen.
share: Abraham weighed out the silver… four hundred shekels (Genesis 23:16). Is there a debt or an unfair dealing I must set right?
He has broken down the dividing wall (Ephesians 2:14). Which wall must come down in my life?
Do you have eyes, and fail to see? (Mark 8:18). Where have I failed to see what Jesus has done for me?
interc: For families divided by property disputes.
For peace between communities, castes and religions in our land.
For those who handle money, that they may be honest.
For hardened hearts, that Christ may soften them.
For all who walk the Way of the Cross today.
pm.close: Father, by the blood of your Son you made peace and gathered us into one household. Make us just in our dealings and reconciled with one another, so that we may celebrate Easter with one heart. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, Ephron offered Abraham the field as a gift, but Abraham said: I will give the price of the field; accept it from me (Genesis 23:13). He weighed out four hundred shekels of silver according to the weights current among the merchants (Genesis 23:16). The first piece of the promised land was bought honestly and in full.

Christ paid a greater price. Paul writes: now in Christ Jesus you who once were far off have been brought near by the blood of Christ. For he is our peace; he has broken down the dividing wall, that is, the hostility between us (Ephesians 2:13–14).

In the boat the disciples had only one loaf, and Jesus warned them: beware of the yeast of the Pharisees and the yeast of Herod (Mark 8:15). Yeast is small and hidden, and it spreads; so do hypocrisy and the hunger for power, in any heart.

Jesus asks: do you not yet understand? (Mark 8:21). The one loaf in the boat was Jesus himself. On this Friday of the Fast, as we walk the Way of the Cross, let us pay what we owe, make peace where there is a wall, and open our eyes to the Lord who gave himself for us. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus is our peace. When people are angry, it is like building a wall between them. Jesus came to break down the walls and make us one family. If you have quarrelled with your brother, sister or a friend, say sorry today and break down the wall!

intro: Abraham's honest purchase, the wall broken down by the blood of Christ, and the one Loaf in the disciples' boat.

sub: Four hundred shekels, weighed in public.
q: I will not offer burnt offerings to the Lord my God that cost me nothing.
For you were bought with a price; therefore glorify God in your body.

sub: Brought near by the blood of Christ.
q: Peace, peace, to the far and the near, says the Lord; and I will heal them.
There is no longer Jew or Greek, there is no longer slave or free, there is no longer male and female; for all of you are one in Christ Jesus.
points.apply: Make peace this week with one person from whom you are estranged.

points.h: The one loaf in the boat
q: Do not harden your hearts, as at Meribah, as on the day at Massah in the wilderness,
Clean out the old yeast so that you may be a new batch, as you really are unleavened. For our paschal lamb, Christ, has been sacrificed.
points.apply: Make the Way of the Cross this Friday and ask Christ to soften your heart.

concl: Abraham paid in silver; Christ paid in his blood to make us one household.
Honest dealings and reconciled hearts prepare us for Easter.
2027-03-12.resolve: Before Easter, settle what you owe and break down one wall of hostility.
